resolvedQuestions.question: What JSON types exist, which are authored versus generated, where are they present for H and S roots, and what automation covers them?
Which fields or files are redundant, unused, duplicated, or drift-prone, and what consolidation has the highest leverage?
Which hand-authored JSON and validation steps could be generated, scaffolded, or automatically checked?
Which metadata and intent signals actually drive advisor routing, and where does routing effectiveness fall short?
Which JSON surfaces lack unit, CI, freshness, scaffold-to-ingest, and end-to-end routing coverage?

keyFindings.summary: Eight governed root JSON filenames split across H and S with class-specific authored/generated status.
The current fleet has seven H and four S roots; all 11 pass root-contract and generated-freshness gates.
graph-metadata.json is authored identity with a separately generated advisor-maintained derived block.
Scaffolds emit authored declarations while the root gate owns derivable manifest and S-alias generation.
The root gate has complete adoption discovery while the older freshness scanner sees committed manifests only.
Advisor watcher/SQLite and compiled activation manifests are projections over root sources.
TypeScript sync and Python compiler define incompatible derived-v2 shapes consumed differently by the scorer.
sk-doc routerPolicy.tieBreak is an already-drifted duplicate ignored in favor of routerSignals key order.
advisorRouting.packetSkillName duplicates consumed top-level packetSkillName without a verified production reader.
Registry aliases and router vocabulary overlap but retain distinct consumers and need explicit ownership.
Standalone aliases are generated identity copies while hub relocation aliases remain load-bearing.
Five hub description fields lack verified local consumers beyond the enforced four-field identity.
Scaffolds stop before producing class-required generated manifests and standalone aliases.
Derived graph metadata has conflicting schemas and the sync writer has no production lifecycle trigger.
Fleet CI does not validate downstream graph ingestibility, edge/path integrity, or derived freshness.
Standalone manifest config is mostly conventional boilerplate suitable for defaults plus overrides.
Hub scaffolding repeats derivable identities across five authored JSON surfaces without reconciliation.
Compiled-route mint/refresh lacks a fleet source-change-to-refresh owner.
Derived key-file watches trigger reindex but unchanged graph metadata prevents candidate projection updates.
Normal root selection consumes SKILL and graph projection fields, not hub registry/router or leaf JSON.
High-specificity hub vocabulary is invisible until parent selection, producing confirmed natural-language misses.
Filesystem fallback retains direct root fields but drops graph edges and doc-trigger projections.
Executor delegation consumes hub aliases but memoizes them without source-change invalidation.
Compiled sk-doc routing is active while committed evaluation supports moderate version-sensitive root accuracy.
Generated artifacts and command metadata have behavior-rich coverage; authored identity lacks one canonical full-schema gate.
No test joins scaffold, generated gate, advisor ingest, root selection, and compiled mode selection.
Failure handling is deep inside stages but does not propagate failures across lifecycle seams.
Filesystem fallback tests prove availability and warnings, not lane or recommendation parity.
Compiled invalidation is guarded; watched-key and delegation-cache invalidation are not.
Canaries cover all command routes but only two positive natural-language routes and no joined per-mode parent cases.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Treat spec-folder metadata generators as skill-root producers
Treat output-first leaf-manifest freshness as complete adoption coverage
Delete compiled activation manifests as duplicate route data
Collapse command metadata into mode registries without a projection
Generate authored H routing semantics from folder structure
Use spec-folder generators for skill-root identity
Treat hub router vocabulary as normal advisor root-selection input
Treat key-file watch activation as derived-content refresh
Redesign scorer weights for upstream metadata activation gaps
Treat fixture presence as behavioral coverage
Treat isolated discovery parity as complete ingest parity
